sections.h2: Missoula and the land under your house
sections.html:
Missoula sits in western Montana, less than 25 miles from the Idaho border, at 3,209 feet. The city covers about 35 square miles on a flat valley floor, with Mount Sentinel and Mount Jumbo rising on its edges. Houses range from older neighborhoods near the river to hillside lots on the slopes.

The land around a Missoula house varies a lot. A river-bottom parcel, a steep-slope lot and a house in a rural fire district outside city limits can all carry different tax bills and raise different buyer questions. Look up your parcel before you list.

Missoula County collects one bill for many bodies that set rates. The County Clerk and Treasurer's office collects for every taxing jurisdiction in the county, so a single bill can include county, city, school, fire, transit and state university levies. The 2026 notice names the six largest you are likely to see:

  • Missoula County Public Schools
  • City of Missoula
  • Missoula County
  • Missoula Urban Transportation District (Mountain Line)
  • Missoula Rural Fire District
  • Montana University System

Special districts for water, sewer, irrigation or bus service can add lines. The county's property tax page lets you search by last name, address, geocode or taxpayer ID and shows a pie chart of how your bill splits among jurisdictions.

The first half of the 2026 bill must be postmarked by Monday, November 30, 2026, and the second half falls due Tuesday, June 1, 2027. Both halves sit on one invoice, and no separate second-half bill is mailed. If you mail a payment between November 26 and 30, hand it to a post office employee and ask for a counter postmark.

Under MCA 15-16-102 the standard dates are 5 p.m. on November 30 and 5 p.m. on May 31, and a weekend or holiday pushes the deadline to the next business day. Primary residences can enroll in a seven-payment schedule running from November 30 through May 31.

Unpaid tax becomes a lien on the house, and it has to be cleared at closing. Taxes go delinquent after the date and time printed on your October or November bill. A 2% penalty applies, and interest runs at 10% annualized (5/6 of 1% a month under state law).

  • Late June or early July: delinquent notices are mailed.
  • First business day in August: the lien attaches, and a $75 tax lien certificate fee is added to the property.
  • Late August: outside investors may buy the lien and take an assignment.
  • The county gives a taxpayer two to three years from the lien date to pay or risk losing the property.

Ask the title company for a payoff figure that includes penalty and interest through the closing date. The delinquent tax comes out of your proceeds, so a house with a lien can still sell, though your net shrinks. A lien that attached in August clears the same way at closing.

sections.h2: The 2026 rate change and empty houses
sections.html:
Under Montana's 2026 structure, a primary residence is taxed at a lower tiered rate than a second home. The tiers are 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value, 0.90% from $378,001 to $756,000, 1.10% from $756,001 to $1,511,999, and 1.90% above that.

A house that is not a primary residence or long-term rental falls under a flat 1.90%, a group that includes second homes, short-term rentals and vacant residential lots. To get the lower rate, an owner must live in the home seven or more months of the year, and a long-term rental must be rented for 28 or more days at a time for at least seven months.

Heirs and landlords should watch this. If you inherit a house and nobody lives there, or a tenant leaves and the unit sits empty, the lower rate may stop applying. The Department of Revenue explains enrollment and refunds on its 2026 property tax page.

The state, not the county or city, values your property, so a dispute starts with the Department of Revenue. Residential property is reappraised every two years, and the county treasurer's page says to file as soon as you get your notice.

You have two routes. Send a Request for Informal Classification and Appraisal Review (Form AB-26) to the department online, or appeal directly to the Missoula County Tax Appeal Board through the online application at mtab.mt.gov/appealform. Your property record card, which lists the buildings and characteristics the state used, is online, so check it for errors before you file.

sections.h2: Paperwork when a Missoula house is sold
sections.html:
Every transfer of real property in Montana needs a Realty Transfer Certificate filed with the county clerk and recorder when the deed is presented for recording. An inaccurate or missing certificate can bring a $500 penalty, six months in jail, or both. Have these ready:

  • The names and mailing addresses of seller and buyer, plus the last four digits of each Social Security number or federal ID number.
  • Whether the property was the seller's principal residence, meaning occupied for at least seven months.
  • The sale price and whether the financing was cash, FHA, VA or contract.
  • A water right disclosure signed by the seller.

Any gain is Montana-source income and should be reported on a return, and the state cross-checks the identification numbers against income tax filings. If the house is on city water, check the public-supply box for the water right. The Missoula office of the Department of Natural Resources and Conservation handles Granite, Mineral, Missoula and Ravalli counties.

sections.h2: When the house needs a roof or furnace
sections.html: Missoula winters are cold and moderately snowy, and summers are hot and dry. Roofing, gutters, furnaces and exterior paint take the strain, and a buyer's inspector will look at all of them. If your house needs a roof or a furnace, a conventional sale can stall at inspection. Selling as is to a cash buyer removes the repair negotiation, though the price will reflect the condition.

faqs.q: What is Missoula property tax and who collects it?
faqs.a: It is a set of levies from the county, city, schools, fire, transit and the university system, all collected by the Missoula County Clerk and Treasurer. The Montana Department of Revenue sets the value, and the county bills it.

faqs.q: When is Missoula property tax due?
faqs.a: The first half of the 2026 bill must be postmarked by Monday, November 30, 2026, and the second half is due Tuesday, June 1, 2027. A deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Missoula house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax, penalty and interest are paid from your proceeds at closing, so the title company needs a current payoff amount. A lien that attached in August can be cleared the same way.

faqs.q: What form do I file when I sell a house in Missoula?
faqs.a: A Realty Transfer Certificate, filed with the Missoula County Clerk and Recorder when the deed is recorded. It covers parties, price, financing, principal residence status and water rights.

faqs.q: Does an empty inherited house in Missoula get the lower tax rate?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The tiered rate is for primary residences and qualifying long-term rentals, and second homes and vacant residential lots pay a flat 1.90%.
